# PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE

## This Practice Direction supplements CPR rule 55.10A.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > This Practice Direction supplements CPR rule 55.10A.] Contents of this Practice Direction

## Scope of this practice direction

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Scope of this practice direction] 1.1 This practice direction provides for a scheme (‘Possession Claims Online’) to operate in the County Court–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Scope of this practice direction] (1) enabling claimants and their representatives to start certain possession claims under CPR Part 55 by requesting the issue of a claim form electronically via the PCOL website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Scope of this practice direction] (2) where a claim has been started electronically, enabling the claimant or defendant and their representatives to take further steps in the claim electronically as specified below.

## 1.2 In this practice direction –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 1.2 In this practice direction –] (1) ‘PCOL website’ means the website which may be accessed via the Business Link website, and through which Possession Claims Online will operate.

## Information on the PCOL website

## 2.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 2.1] The PCOL website contains further details and guidance about the operation of Possession Claims Online.

## 2.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 2.2] In particular the PCOL website sets out –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 2.2] (1) the specified courts; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 2.2] (2) the dates from which Possession Claims Online will be available in each specified court.

## 2.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 2.3] The operation of Possession Claims Online in any specified court may be restricted to taking certain of the steps specified in this practice direction, and in such cases the PCOL website will set out the steps which may be taken using Possession Claims Online in that specified court.

## Security

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Security] 3.1 HM Courts and Tribunals Service will take such measures as it thinks fit to ensure the security of steps taken or information stored electronically. These may include requiring users of Possession Claims Online –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Security] (1) to enter a customer identification number or password;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Security] (2) to provide personal information for identification purposes; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Security] (3) to comply with any other security measures,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Security] before taking any step online.

## Fees

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Fees] 4.1 A step may only be taken using Possession Claims Online on payment of the prescribed fee where a fee is payable. Where this practice direction provides for a fee to be paid electronically, it may be paid by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Fees] (1) credit card;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Fees] (2) debit card; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Fees] (3) any other method which HM Courts and Tribunals Service may permit.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Fees] 4.2 A defendant who wishes to claim exemption from payment of fees must do so through an organisation approved by HM Courts and Tribunals Service before taking any step using PCOL which attracts a fee. If satisfied that the defendant is entitled to fee exemption, the organisation will submit the fee exemption form through the PCOL website to HM Courts and Tribunals Service. The defendant may then use PCOL to take such a step.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Fees] (HM Courts and Tribunals Service website contains guidance as to when the entitlement to claim an exemption from payment of fees arises. The PCOL website will contain a list of organisations through which the defendant may claim an exemption from fees).

## Claims which may be started using Possession Claims Online

## 5.1 A claim may be started online if –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (1) it is brought under Sections I or IV of Part 55;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (2) it includes a possession claim for residential property or a Renting Homes possession claim by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (a) a landlord against a tenant or contract holder, solely on the ground of arrears of rent (but not a claim for forfeiture of a lease); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (b) a mortgagee against a mortgagor, solely on the ground of default in the payment of sums due under a mortgage,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] relating to land the address for which is served by a County Court hearing centre;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (3) it does not include a claim for any other remedy except for payment of arrears of rent or money due under a mortgage, interest and costs;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (3A) the claimant has an address for service in the United Kingdom;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (4) the defendant has an address for service in England and Wales; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 5.1 A claim may be started online if –] (5) the claimant is able to provide a postcode for the property.

## 5.2 A claim must not be started online if a defendant is known to be a child or protected party.

## Starting a claim

## 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (1) completing an online claim form at the PCOL website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (2) paying the appropriate issue fee electronically at the PCOL website or by some other means approved by HM Courts and Tribunals Service.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] 6.2 The particulars of claim must be included in the online claim form and may not be filed separately. It is not necessary to file a copy of the tenancy agreement occupation contract, mortgage deed or mortgage agreement with the particulars of claim.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] 6.2A In the case of a possession claim for residential property or a renting homes possession claim that relies on a statutory ground or grounds for possession, the claimant must specify, in section 4(a) of the online claim form, the ground or grounds relied on.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] 6.3 Subject to paragraphs 6.3A and 6.3B, the particulars of claim must include a history of the rent or mortgage account, in schedule form setting out –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (1) the dates and amounts of all payments due and payments made under the tenancy agreement occupation contract, mortgage deed or mortgage agreement either from the first date of default if that date occurred less than two years before the date of issue or for a period of two years immediately preceding the date of issue; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (2) a running total of the arrears.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] 6.3A Paragraph 6.3B applies where the claimant has, before commencing proceedings, provided the defendant in schedule form with–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (1) details of the dates and amounts of all payments due and payments made under the tenancy agreement occupation contract, mortgage deed or mortgage account –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (a) for a period of two years immediately preceding the date of commencing proceedings; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (b) if the first date of default occurred less than two years before that date, from the first date of default; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (2) a running total of the arrears.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] 6.3B Where this paragraph applies the claimant may, in place of the information required by paragraph 6.3, include in his particulars of claim a summary only of the arrears containing at least the following information –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (1) the amount of arrears –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (a) as stated in the notice served –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (i) under section 83 of the Housing Act 1985;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (ii) under section 8 of the Housing Act 1988; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (iii) under section 159, 182 or 188 of the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (b) as at the date of the claimant’s letter before action, as appropriate;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (2) the dates and amounts of the last three payments in cleared funds made by the defendant or, if less than three payments have been made, the dates and amounts of all payments made;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.1 A claimant may request the issue of a claim form by–] (3) the arrears at the date of issue, assuming that no further payments are made by the defendant.

## 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] (1) serve on the defendant not more than 7 days after the date of issue, a full, up-to-date arrears history containing at least the information required by paragraph 6.3; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] (2) either –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] (a) make a witness statement confirming that he has complied with sub-paragraph (1) or (2) of paragraph 6.3A as appropriate, and including or exhibiting the full arrears history; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] (b) verify by way of oral evidence at the hearing that he has complied with sub-paragraph (1) or (2) of paragraph 6.3A as appropriate and also produce and verify the full arrears history.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] (Rules 55.8(4) and 55.36(4) requires all witness statements to be filed and served at least 2 days before the hearing.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] 6.4 If the claimant wishes to rely on a history of arrears which is longer than two years, he should state this in his particulars and exhibit a full (or longer) schedule to a witness statement.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] 6.5 When an online claim form is received, an acknowledgment of receipt will automatically be sent to the claimant. The acknowledgment does not constitute notice that the claim form has been issued or served.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.3C Where the particulars of claim include a summary only of the arrears the claimant must –] 6.6 When the court issues a claim form following the submission of an online claim form, the claim is ‘brought’ for the purposes of the Limitation Act 1980 and any other enactment on the date on which the online claim form is received by the court’s computer system. The court will keep a record, by electronic or other means, of when online claim forms are received.

## 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –] (1) serve a printed version of the claim form and a defence form on the defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –] (2) send the claimant notice of issue by post or, where the claimant has supplied an e-mail address, by electronic means.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –] 6.8 The claim shall be deemed to be served on the fifth day after the claim was issued irrespective of whether that day is a business day or not.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –] 6.9 Where the period of time within which a defence must be filed ends on a day when the court is closed, the defendant may file his defence on the next day that the court is open.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –] 6.10 The claim form shall have printed on it a unique customer identification number or a password by which the defendant may access the claim on the PCOL website.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –] 6.11 PCOL will issue the proceedings in the appropriate County Court hearing centre by reference to the post code provided by the claimant and that court shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine the claim and to carry out enforcement of any judgment irrespective of whether the property is within or outside the jurisdiction of that court.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 6.7 When the court issues a claim form it will –] (CPR 30.2(1) authorises proceedings to be transferred from one County Court to another.)

## Defence

## 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –] (1) a defence; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –] (2) a counterclaim (to be filed together with a defence) to a claim which has been issued through the PCOL system,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –] may, instead of filing a written form, do so by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –] (a) completing the relevant online form at the PCOL website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –] (b) if the defendant is making a counterclaim, paying the appropriate fee electronically at the PCOL website or by some other means approved by HM Courts and Tribunals Service.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –] 7.2 Where a defendant files a defence by completing the relevant online form, he must not send the court a hard copy.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.1 A defendant wishing to file –] 7.3 When an online defence form is received, an acknowledgment of receipt will automatically be sent to the defendant. The acknowledgment does not constitute notice that the defence has been served.

## 7.4 The online defence form will be treated as being filed –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.4 The online defence form will be treated as being filed –] (1) on the day the court receives it, if it receives it before 4 p.m. on a working day; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.4 The online defence form will be treated as being filed –] (2) otherwise, on the next working day after the court receives the online defence form.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 7.4 The online defence form will be treated as being filed –] 7.5 A defence is filed when the online defence form is received by the court’s computer system. The court will keep a record, by electronic or other means, of when online defence forms are received.

## Statement of truth

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Statement of truth] 8.1 CPR Part 22 requires any statement of case to be verified by a statement of truth. This applies to any online claims and defences and application notices.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Statement of truth] 8.2 CPR Part 22 also requires that if an applicant wishes to rely on matters set out in his application notice as evidence, the application notice must be verified by a statement of truth. This applies to any application notice completed online that contains matters on which the applicant wishes to rely as evidence.

## 8.3 Attention is drawn to –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 8.3 Attention is drawn to –] (1) paragraph 2 of Practice Direction 22, which stipulates the form of the statement of truth; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 8.3 Attention is drawn to –] (2)  rule 22.1(6) and paragraph 3 of Practice Direction 22, which provides who may sign a statement of truth; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 8.3 Attention is drawn to –] (3) CPR 32.14, which sets out the consequences of making, or causing to be made, a false statement in a document verified by a statement of truth, without an honest belief in its truth.

## Signature

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Signature] 9.1 Any provision of the CPR which requires a document to be signed by any person is satisfied by that person entering his name on an online form.

## Communication with the court electronically by the messaging service

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Communication with the court electronically by the messaging service] 10.1 If the PCOL website specifies that a court accepts electronic communications relating to claims brought using Possession Claims Online the parties may communicate with the court using the messaging service facility, available on the PCOL website (‘the messaging service’).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Communication with the court electronically by the messaging service] 10.2 The messaging service is for brief and straightforward communications only. The PCOL website contains a list of examples of when it will not be appropriate to use the messaging service.

## 10.3 Parties must not send to the court forms or attachments via the messaging service.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 10.3 Parties must not send to the court forms or attachments via the messaging service.] 10.4 The court shall treat any forms or attachments sent via the messaging service as not having been filed or received.

## 10.5 The court will normally reply via the messaging service where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 10.5 The court will normally reply via the messaging service where –] (1) the response is to a message transmitted via the messaging service; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 10.5 The court will normally reply via the messaging service where –] (2) the sender has provided an e-mail address.

## Electronic applications

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Electronic applications] 11.1 Certain applications in relation to a possession claim or Renting Homes possession claim started online may be made electronically (‘online applications’). An online application may be made if a form for that application is published on the PCOL website (‘online application form’) and the application is made at least five clear days before the hearing.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Electronic applications] 11.2 If a claim for possession has been started online and a party wishes to make an online application, he may do so by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Electronic applications] (1) completing the appropriate online application form at the PCOL website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Electronic applications] (2) paying the appropriate fee electronically at the PCOL website or by some other means approved by HM Courts and Tribunals Service.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Electronic applications] 11.3 When an online application form is received, an acknowledgment of receipt will automatically be sent to the applicant. The acknowledgment does not constitute a notice that the online application form has been issued or served.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Electronic applications] 11.4 Where an application must be made within a specified time, it is so made if the online application form is received by the court’s computer system within that time. The court will keep a record, by electronic or other means, of when online application forms are received.

## 11.5 When the court receives an online application form it shall –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 11.5 When the court receives an online application form it shall –] (1) serve a copy of the online application endorsed with the date of the hearing by post on the claimant at least two clear days before the hearing; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 11.5 When the court receives an online application form it shall –] (2) send the defendant notice of service and confirmation of the date of the hearing by post; provided that

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 11.5 When the court receives an online application form it shall –] (3) where either party has provided the court with an e-mail address for service, service of the application and/or the notice of service and confirmation of the hearing date may be effected by electronic means.

## Request for issue of warrant

## 12.1 Where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 12.1 Where –] (1) the court has made an order for possession in a claim started online; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 12.1 Where –] (2) the claimant is entitled to the issue of a warrant of possession without requiring the permission of the court

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 12.1 Where –] the claimant may request the issue of a warrant by completing an online request form at the PCOL website and paying the appropriate fee electronically at the PCOL website or by some other means approved by HM Courts and Tribunals Service.

## 12.2 A request under paragraph 12.1 will be treated as being filed –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 12.2 A request under paragraph 12.1 will be treated as being filed –] (1) on the day the court receives the request, if it receives it before 4 p.m. on a working day; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 12.2 A request under paragraph 12.1 will be treated as being filed –] (2) otherwise, on the next working day after the court receives the request.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 12.2 A request under paragraph 12.1 will be treated as being filed –] (Rule 83.2 sets out certain circumstances in which a warrant of possession may not be issued without the permission of the court.)

## Application to suspend warrant of possession

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Application to suspend warrant of possession] 13.1 Where the court has issued a warrant of possession, the defendant may apply electronically for the suspension of the warrant, provided that:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Application to suspend warrant of possession] (1) the application is made at least five clear days before the appointment for possession; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > Application to suspend warrant of possession] (2) the defendant is not prevented from making such an application without the permission of the court.

## 13.2 The defendant may apply electronically for the suspension of the warrant, by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 13.2 The defendant may apply electronically for the suspension of the warrant, by –] (1) completing an online application for suspension at the PCOL website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 13.2 The defendant may apply electronically for the suspension of the warrant, by –] (2) paying the appropriate fee electronically at the PCOL website or by some other means approved by HM Courts and Tribunals Service.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 13.2 The defendant may apply electronically for the suspension of the warrant, by –] 13.3 When an online application for suspension is received, an acknowledgment of receipt will automatically be sent to the defendant. The acknowledgment does not constitute a notice that the online application for suspension has been served.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 13.2 The defendant may apply electronically for the suspension of the warrant, by –] 13.4 Where an application must be made within a specified time, it is so made if the online application for suspension is received by the court’s computer system within that time. The court will keep a record, by electronic or other means, of when online applications for suspension are received.

## 13.5 When the court receives an online application for suspension it shall –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 13.5 When the court receives an online application for suspension it shall –] (1) serve a copy of the online application for suspension endorsed with the date of the hearing by post on the claimant at least two clear days before the hearing; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 13.5 When the court receives an online application for suspension it shall –] (2) send the defendant notice of service and confirmation of the date of the hearing by post; provided that

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 13.5 When the court receives an online application for suspension it shall –] (3) where either party has provided the court with an e-mail address for service, service of the application and/or the notice of service and confirmation of the hearing date may be effected by electronic means.

## Viewing the case record

## 14.1 A facility will be provided on the PCOL website for parties or their representatives to view –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 14.1 A facility will be provided on the PCOL website for parties or their representatives to view –] (1) an electronic record of the status of claims started online, which will be reviewed and, if necessary, updated at least once each day; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 14.1 A facility will be provided on the PCOL website for parties or their representatives to view –] (2) all information relating to the case that has been filed by the parties electronically.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 14.1 A facility will be provided on the PCOL website for parties or their representatives to view –] 14.2 In addition, where the PCOL website specifies that the court has the facility to provide viewing of such information by electronic means, the parties or their representatives may view the following information electronically –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 14.1 A facility will be provided on the PCOL website for parties or their representatives to view –] (1) court orders made in relation to the case; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 55B – POSSESSION CLAIMS ONLINE > 14.1 A facility will be provided on the PCOL website for parties or their representatives to view –] (2) details of progress on enforcement and subsequent orders made.
category: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions
